scope: Exodus 35–40, all 214 public verses. Prior revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew numbering align throughout Exodus 35–40.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive, textual, social, or versification choice. Editorial assessments are separate from similarity scores. Independent review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Retains Moses gathering entire community and command attribution, opening connected address.
verses.before: Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel and said to them, “These are the things that the LORD has commanded you to do:
verses.after: Moses gathered the whole Israelite community and told them, “These are the things the LORD has commanded you to do.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel and said to them, “These are the things that the LORD has commanded you to do:

verses.rationale: Preserves six/seventh contrast, holiness and explicit death penalty, matching complete rest terminology in 31:15.
verses.before: Six days work will be done, but on the seventh day you will have a holy day, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Whoever does work on it will be put to death.
verses.after: Work may be done for six days, but the seventh must be holy to you, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Anyone who works on it must be put to death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Six days work shall be done, but on the seventh day you shall have a holy day, a Sabbath of complete rest to the LORD. Whoever does work on it shall be put to death.

verses.rationale: Retains comprehensive dwelling scope and specific kindling prohibition without adding exceptions.
verses.before: You will not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”
verses.after: Do not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”
verses.tsw_comparator: You shall not kindle a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day.”

verses.rationale: Keeps renewed speech introduction before contribution commands.
verses.before: Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, “This is the thing that the LORD commanded, saying:
verses.after: Moses told the whole Israelite community, “This is what the LORD has commanded:
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses spoke to all the congregation of the children of Israel, saying, “This is the thing that the LORD commanded, saying:

verses.rationale: Preserves willing-heart agency, repeated contribution and ordered metals, introducing list across labels.
verses.before: Take from among yourselves an offering for the LORD. Everyone whose heart is willing will bring it as the LORD’s offering: gold, silver, and bronze;
verses.after: Take up a contribution to the LORD from among yourselves. Everyone with a willing heart is to bring the LORD’s contribution: gold, silver, and bronze;
verses.tsw_comparator: Take from among yourselves an offering for the LORD. Everyone whose heart is willing shall bring it as the LORD’s offering: gold, silver, and bronze;

verses.rationale: Retains three colors and distinct linen/goat materials without mechanical textile substitution.
verses.before: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats’ hair;
verses.after: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, and goat hair;
verses.tsw_comparator: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn; fine linen and goats’ hair;

verses.rationale: Keeps uncertain taḥash untranslated and red-treated skin convention from 25:5; exact annotated source retained.
verses.before: ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;
verses.after: rams’ skins dyed red, taḥash skins, and acacia wood;
verses.tsw_comparator: ram skins dyed red, fine leather, and acacia wood;

verses.rationale: Preserves separate lighting and aromatic uses in continuing list.
verses.before: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;
verses.after: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and the fragrant incense;
verses.tsw_comparator: oil for the light, spices for the anointing oil and for the fragrant incense;

verses.rationale: Uses provisional onyx convention and preserves distinct garment settings.
verses.before: onyx stones and stones for setting in the ephod and in the breastpiece.
verses.after: and onyx stones and stones to be set in the ephod and breastpiece.
verses.tsw_comparator: onyx stones and stones for setting in the ephod and in the breastpiece.

verses.rationale: Keeps inclusive skill summons and all-command scope, introducing second complete inventory.
verses.before: “Let every wise-hearted person among you come and make all that the LORD has commanded:
verses.after: Let every skilled worker among you come and make everything the LORD has commanded:
verses.tsw_comparator: “Let every wise-hearted person among you come and make all that the LORD has commanded:

verses.rationale: Preserves all eight structural components and exact original annotation; aligns technical nouns with chapter 26.
verses.before: the dwelling, its tent and covering, its clasps, frames, crossbars, pillars, and bases;
verses.after: the tabernacle, its tent and covering, its clasps, frames, crossbars, pillars, and bases;
verses.tsw_comparator: the dwelling, its tent and covering, its clasps, frames, crossbars, pillars, and bases;

verses.rationale: Retains four ark-related components and screening function without inventing placement detail.
verses.before: the ark and its poles, the cover, and the screening veil;
verses.after: the ark and its poles, the atonement cover, and the curtain that screens it;
verses.tsw_comparator: the ark and its poles, the cover, and the screening veil;

verses.rationale: Keeps bread distinct from table hardware and retains learned biblical term.
verses.before: the table and its poles, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
verses.after: the table, its poles and all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;
verses.tsw_comparator: the table and its poles, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence;

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated light language, lamps and utensils separately.
verses.before: the lampstand for the light, its utensils and lamps, and the oil for the light;
verses.after: the lampstand for the light, its utensils and lamps, and the oil for the light;
verses.tsw_comparator: the lampstand for the light, its utensils and lamps, and the oil for the light;

verses.rationale: Keeps aromatic objects and entrance screen in their source list position.
verses.before: the altar of incense and its poles, the anointing oil and fragrant incense, and the entrance screen for the entrance of the dwelling;
verses.after: the incense altar and its poles, the anointing oil and fragrant incense, and the entrance screen for the tabernacle;
verses.tsw_comparator: the altar of incense and its poles, the anointing oil and fragrant incense, and the entrance screen for the entrance of the dwelling;

verses.rationale: Retains all altar equipment and separate basin/stand, bronze specificity.
verses.before: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin and its stand;
verses.after: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grating, poles, and all its utensils, and the basin with its stand;
verses.tsw_comparator: the altar of burnt offering with its bronze grate, its poles, and all its utensils; the basin and its stand;

verses.rationale: Retains courtyard components without confusing its screen with tent entrance.
verses.before: the hangings of the court, its pillars and bases, and the screen for the gate of the court;
verses.after: the courtyard hangings, its pillars and bases, and the screen at the courtyard entrance;
verses.tsw_comparator: the hangings of the court, its pillars and bases, and the screen for the gate of the court;

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated peg locations and ropes instead of reducing to generic fasteners.
verses.before: the pegs of the dwelling and the pegs of the court and their cords;
verses.after: the tabernacle’s tent pegs, the courtyard’s tent pegs, and their ropes;
verses.tsw_comparator: the pegs of the dwelling and the pegs of the court and their cords;

verses.rationale: Retains three garment descriptions and named priestly family; uncertain service-garment term follows 31:10.
verses.before: the woven garments for ministering in the Holy Place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for priestly service.”
verses.after: and the garments for service in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and his sons’ garments for serving as priests.”
verses.tsw_comparator: the woven garments for ministering in the Holy Place, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons for priestly service.”

verses.rationale: Retains whole-community departure before individual contributions.
verses.before: Then all the congregation of the children of Israel went out from before Moses.
verses.after: Then the whole Israelite community left Moses’ presence.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the congregation of the children of Israel went out from before Moses.

verses.rationale: Preserves heart and spirit as distinct motives and all three uses of contributions.
verses.before: Everyone whose heart lifted him and everyone whose spirit moved him came and brought the LORD’s offering for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
verses.after: Everyone whose heart moved them and whose spirit made them willing came with a contribution to the LORD for the work on the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone whose heart lifted him and everyone whose spirit moved him came and brought the LORD’s offering for the work of the tent of meeting, for all its service, and for the holy garments.

verses.rationale: Retains women alongside men and four traditional ornament categories; does not treat donors as male-only or resolve uncertain ornament forms.
verses.before: They came, men along with women, everyone willing of heart, bringing brooches, earrings, rings, and ornaments, all kinds of gold objects; everyone who waved a wave offering of gold to the LORD.
verses.after: Men came along with women, all with willing hearts. They brought brooches, earrings, rings, and pendants—every kind of gold ornament. All who presented a gold offering to the LORD came.
verses.tsw_comparator: They came, men along with women, everyone willing of heart, bringing brooches, earrings, rings, and ornaments, all kinds of gold objects; everyone who waved a wave offering of gold to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserves full seven-material contribution list and recurring uncertain skin term.
verses.before: Everyone with whom was found blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, ram skins dyed red, or fine leather brought them.
verses.after: Everyone who had blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, fine linen, goat hair, rams’ skins dyed red, or taḥash skins brought them.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone with whom was found blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, ram skins dyed red, or fine leather brought them.

verses.rationale: Keeps metal and wood donors separately and repeated bringing action.
verses.before: Everyone who lifted up a contribution of silver or bronze brought the LORD’s offering, and everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service brought it.
verses.after: Everyone contributing silver or bronze brought it as the LORD’s contribution. Everyone who had acacia wood for any part of the work brought it.
verses.tsw_comparator: Everyone who lifted up a contribution of silver or bronze brought the LORD’s offering, and everyone with whom was found acacia wood for any work of the service brought it.

verses.rationale: Retains specifically female skilled labor, hands, and four spun materials without erasing expertise into generic help.
verses.before: Every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and the fine linen.
verses.after: Every skilled woman spun with her own hands and brought what she had spun: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every wise-hearted woman spun with her hands and brought what she had spun: the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and the fine linen.

verses.rationale: Keeps women’s heart-led skilled contribution and separate goat-hair production.
verses.before: All the women whose hearts lifted them in wisdom spun the goats’ hair.
verses.after: All the women whose hearts moved them to use their skill spun the goat hair.
verses.tsw_comparator: All the women whose hearts lifted them in wisdom spun the goats’ hair.

verses.rationale: Preserves leaders’ distinct contribution and list continuing into next verse.
verses.before: The leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting in the ephod and breastpiece,
verses.after: The leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones to be set in the ephod and breastpiece,
verses.tsw_comparator: The leaders brought the onyx stones and the stones for setting in the ephod and breastpiece,

verses.rationale: Maintains leaders as agents across label and all three aromatic/lighting uses.
verses.before: and the spices and oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.
verses.after: as well as the spices and oil for the light, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the spices and oil for the light, for the anointing oil, and for the fragrant incense.

verses.rationale: Preserves explicit men/women and summary freewill contribution under divine command through Moses.
verses.before: Every man and woman among the children of Israel whose heart moved them to bring something for all the work that the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.
verses.after: Every man and woman whose heart made them willing to bring something for all the work the LORD had commanded through Moses did so. The Israelites brought a freewill offering to the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every man and woman among the children of Israel whose heart moved them to bring something for all the work that the LORD had commanded by the hand of Moses brought it as a freewill offering to the LORD.

verses.rationale: Retains named artisan, both paternal links and tribal identity with call-by-name echo.
verses.before: Moses said to the children of Israel, “See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
verses.after: Moses told the Israelites, “Look, the LORD has called Bezalel by name, the son of Uri, the son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses said to the children of Israel, “See, the LORD has called by name Bezalel son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.

verses.rationale: Keeps Spirit and ordered qualities tied to craft; matches chapter 31 terminology.
verses.before: He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of craftsmanship,
verses.after: He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill in every kind of craft,
verses.tsw_comparator: He has filled him with the Spirit of God, with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and every kind of craftsmanship,

verses.rationale: Retains design and three-metal work as purpose continuation.
verses.before: to devise skilled designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
verses.after: to devise designs and work in gold, silver, and bronze,
verses.tsw_comparator: to devise skilled designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,

verses.rationale: Preserves stone setting, wood carving and comprehensive design ability without adding unmentioned crafts.
verses.before: in cutting stones for setting, in carving wood, and in doing every kind of skilled work.
verses.after: to cut stones for settings, to carve wood, and to carry out every kind of skilled design.
verses.tsw_comparator: in cutting stones for setting, in carving wood, and in doing every kind of skilled work.

verses.rationale: Clarifies teaching ability granted to both named men while preserving Oholiab’s father and tribe.
verses.before: He has also put in his heart the ability to teach, both he and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan.
verses.after: He has given Bezalel the ability to teach, and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, has received this too.
verses.tsw_comparator: He has also put in his heart the ability to teach, both he and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan.

verses.rationale: Retains distinct craft roles, embroidery materials and repeated breadth of skill in readable two-sentence conclusion.
verses.before: He has filled them with wisdom of heart to do every kind of work: engraving, skilled design, embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and weaving—workers of every kind and designers of skillful work.
verses.after: God has filled them with skill to do every kind of work: engraving, designing, embroidering in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and weaving. They can carry out every kind of craft and devise designs.”
verses.tsw_comparator: He has filled them with wisdom of heart to do every kind of work: engraving, skilled design, embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, and weaving—workers of every kind and designers of skillful work.

verses.rationale: Reads verse as continuation of Moses’ instruction, not premature completion report; retains divine enabling and command standard.
verses.before: Bezalel, Oholiab, and every wise-hearted person in whom the LORD had put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of the service of the sanctuary will work according to all that the LORD has commanded.
verses.after: “Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled worker to whom the LORD has given wisdom and understanding are to carry out all the work of the sanctuary’s service, knowing how to do it just as the LORD has commanded.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Bezalel, Oholiab, and every wise-hearted person in whom the LORD had put wisdom and understanding to know how to do all the work of the service of the sanctuary shall work according to all that the LORD has commanded.

verses.rationale: Retains named leaders, divine wisdom and voluntary heart motive with exact source annotation.
verses.before: Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab, and every wise-hearted person in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, everyone whose heart lifted him to come near to the work to do it.
verses.after: Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled worker in whose heart the LORD had placed wisdom—everyone whose heart moved them to come forward and do the work.
verses.tsw_comparator: Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab, and every wise-hearted person in whose heart the LORD had put wisdom, everyone whose heart lifted him to come near to the work to do it.

verses.rationale: Distinguishes workers receiving from Moses and continuing people’s donations with repeated morning cadence.
verses.before: They received from before Moses all the offering that the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to do it. And the people continued bringing him freewill offerings morning by morning.
verses.after: They received from Moses all the contributions the Israelites had brought for carrying out the sanctuary’s work. Yet the people kept bringing him freewill offerings morning after morning.
verses.tsw_comparator: They received from before Moses all the offering that the children of Israel had brought for the work of the service of the sanctuary, to do it. And the people continued bringing him freewill offerings morning by morning.

verses.rationale: Retains all workers individually interrupting their tasks and continues speech connection.
verses.before: Then all the wise people doing all the work of the sanctuary came, each from the work he was doing,
verses.after: Then all the skilled workers doing the sanctuary’s work came, each leaving the work they were doing,
verses.tsw_comparator: Then all the wise people doing all the work of the sanctuary came, each from the work he was doing,

verses.rationale: Keeps excess relative to commanded task, without inserting fundraising application.
verses.before: and they said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for the service of the work that the LORD commanded to be done.”
verses.after: and told Moses, “The people are bringing more than is needed to carry out the work the LORD commanded.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and they said to Moses, “The people are bringing more than enough for the service of the work that the LORD commanded to be done.”

verses.rationale: Preserves both genders, making prohibition and resulting restraint of contributions.
verses.before: So Moses commanded, and they caused a proclamation to pass throughout the camp, saying, “Let no man or woman do any more work for the offering of the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing.
verses.after: So Moses ordered a proclamation throughout the camp: “No man or woman is to make anything more as a contribution for the sanctuary.” In this way the people were stopped from bringing more.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Moses commanded, and they caused a proclamation to pass throughout the camp, saying, “Let no man or woman do any more work for the offering of the sanctuary.” So the people were restrained from bringing.

verses.rationale: Keeps sufficiency and surplus as two connected claims.
verses.before: For the material they had was enough for all the work to do it, and more than enough.
verses.after: What they had was enough to do all the work, with some left over.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the material they had was enough for all the work to do it, and more than enough.

verses.rationale: Uses craftsman for the unnamed singular maker following plural workers; keeps ten curtains, materials and cherubim.
verses.before: Every wise-hearted person among those doing the work made the dwelling with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. With cherubim, the work of a skilled designer, he made them.
verses.after: All the skilled workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. The craftsman worked cherubim into their design.
verses.tsw_comparator: Every wise-hearted person among those doing the work made the dwelling with ten curtains of fine twisted linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn. With cherubim, the work of a skilled designer, he made them.

verses.rationale: Retains exact size and common-dimension statement rather than approximate modern conversions.
verses.before: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits and the width of each curtain four cubits. All the curtains had the same measure.
verses.after: Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All the curtains had the same dimensions.
verses.tsw_comparator: The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits and the width of each curtain four cubits. All the curtains had the same measure.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated joining and two five-curtain sets.
verses.before: He joined five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he joined to one another.
verses.after: He joined five curtains to one another, and joined the other five to one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: He joined five curtains to one another, and the other five curtains he joined to one another.

verses.rationale: Clarifies facing end curtains and identical loop placement without inventing attachment count here.
verses.before: He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the outer curtain in the first set, and likewise on the edge of the outer curtain in the second set.
verses.after: He made blue loops along the edge of the end curtain in the first set, and did the same along the end curtain in the second set.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made loops of blue yarn on the edge of the outer curtain in the first set, and likewise on the edge of the outer curtain in the second set.

verses.rationale: Preserves fifty repeated for each facing curtain rather than collapsing to total hundred.
verses.before: He made fifty loops on the first curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, the loops opposite one another.
verses.after: He made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain in the second set, with the loops facing one another.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made fifty loops on the first curtain and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set, the loops opposite one another.

verses.rationale: Keeps material, count, joining and unity result matching chapter 26 instruction.
verses.before: He made fifty clasps of gold and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the dwelling became one.
verses.after: He made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to one another with them, so the tabernacle formed one whole.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made fifty clasps of gold and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the dwelling became one.

verses.rationale: Retains eleven distinct outer curtains and over-tabernacle relation.
verses.before: He made curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the dwelling; eleven curtains he made.
verses.after: He made eleven goat-hair curtains for a tent over the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made curtains of goats’ hair for a tent over the dwelling; eleven curtains he made.

verses.rationale: Preserves outer curtain length difference from inner layer and all-eleven uniformity.
verses.before: The length of each curtain was thirty cubits and the width of each curtain four cubits. The eleven curtains had the same measure.
verses.after: Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven curtains had the same dimensions.
verses.tsw_comparator: The length of each curtain was thirty cubits and the width of each curtain four cubits. The eleven curtains had the same measure.

verses.rationale: Keeps asymmetric grouping rather than regularizing to two equal sets.
verses.before: He joined five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves.
verses.after: He joined five curtains into one set and six into another.
verses.tsw_comparator: He joined five curtains by themselves and six curtains by themselves.

verses.rationale: Retains both fifty counts and joining-edge relationships.
verses.before: He made fifty loops on the edge of the outer curtain in the first set and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set.
verses.after: He made fifty loops along the edge of the end curtain in one set and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain in the second set.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made fifty loops on the edge of the outer curtain in the first set and fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in the second set.

verses.rationale: Preserves bronze contrast with inner gold fasteners and unity formula.
verses.before: He made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together so that it became one.
verses.after: He made fifty bronze clasps to join the tent together as one whole.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made fifty clasps of bronze to join the tent together so that it became one.

verses.rationale: Keeps two outer covering layers and uncertainty of skin identification.
verses.before: He made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red and a covering of fine leather above it.
verses.after: He made a covering for the tent from rams’ skins dyed red, with a covering of taḥash skins above it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made a covering for the tent of ram skins dyed red and a covering of fine leather above it.

verses.rationale: Uses provisional frames rather than forcing solid boards; preserves upright posture and acacia.
verses.before: He made upright frames of acacia wood for the dwelling.
verses.after: He made upright frames of acacia wood for the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made upright frames of acacia wood for the dwelling.

verses.rationale: Keeps exact repeated upright dimensions.
verses.before: Ten cubits was the length of a frame and a cubit and a half the width of each frame.
verses.after: Each frame was ten cubits long and a cubit and a half wide.
verses.tsw_comparator: Ten cubits was the length of a frame and a cubit and a half the width of each frame.

verses.rationale: Renders projecting hands as tenons with uncertainty in note; retains two and uniform manufacture.
verses.before: Each frame had two tenons joined to one another. Thus he made all the frames of the dwelling.
verses.after: Each frame had two tenons fitted alongside one another. He made all the tabernacle’s frames this way.
verses.tsw_comparator: Each frame had two tenons joined to one another. Thus he made all the frames of the dwelling.

verses.rationale: Preserves twenty and southern orientation.
verses.before: He made the frames for the dwelling: twenty frames for the south side,
verses.after: He made twenty frames for the tabernacle’s south side.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the frames for the dwelling: twenty frames for the south side,

verses.rationale: Retains forty/twenty and repeated two-base/two-tenon formula, rather than collapsing redundant source detail.
verses.before: and he made forty silver bases under the twenty frames, two bases under one frame for its two tenons and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.
verses.after: He made forty silver bases beneath the twenty frames: two bases beneath one frame for its two tenons, and two beneath the next for its two tenons.
verses.tsw_comparator: and he made forty silver bases under the twenty frames, two bases under one frame for its two tenons and two bases under the next frame for its two tenons.

verses.rationale: Keeps other-side orientation and twenty count in sentence spanning next label.
verses.before: For the second side of the dwelling, the north side, he made twenty frames,
verses.after: For the tabernacle’s other side, the north, he made twenty frames,
verses.tsw_comparator: For the second side of the dwelling, the north side, he made twenty frames,

verses.rationale: Preserves forty silver bases and paired distribution without adding tenons absent here.
verses.before: with their forty silver bases, two bases under one frame and two bases under the next frame.
verses.after: with forty silver bases: two bases beneath one frame and two beneath the next.
verses.tsw_comparator: with their forty silver bases, two bases under one frame and two bases under the next frame.

verses.rationale: Retains rear/west relation and six distinct from added corners.
verses.before: For the rear of the dwelling westward he made six frames.
verses.after: For the back of the tabernacle, toward the west, he made six frames.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the rear of the dwelling westward he made six frames.

verses.rationale: Preserves two additional corner frames without combining prematurely into eight.
verses.before: He made two frames for the corners of the dwelling at the rear.
verses.after: He made two more frames for the corners at the back of the tabernacle.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made two frames for the corners of the dwelling at the rear.

verses.rationale: Retains difficult bottom/top/ring construction with qualified note rather than inventing complete engineering plan.
verses.before: They were doubled below and together complete at the top to the first ring. Thus he made both of them for the two corners.
verses.after: They were paired at the bottom and joined together at the top, at one ring. He made both corner frames this way.

verses.rationale: Keeps material and initial five while allowing list across verse boundary.

verses.after: He made poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

verses.after: He made the table from acacia wood, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and a cubit and a half high.

verses.rationale: Preserves purity and surrounding molding parallel with ark.
verses.before: He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.
verses.after: He overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.

verses.rationale: Keeps explicit table-carrying purpose, wood and gold.

verses.rationale: Preserves all four vessel classes in source order, differing order from 25:29; shapes remain provisional.

verses.tsw_comparator: He made the utensils that were on the table—its plates, dishes, bowls, and pitchers with which to pour drink offerings—of pure gold.

verses.rationale: Retains hammered manufacture and all five integral components.

verses.after: He made the lampstand from pure gold, hammering it into shape. Its base, shaft, cups, buds, and flowers were all of one piece with it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the lampstand of pure gold. He made the lampstand of hammered work; its base and shaft, its cups, buds, and blossoms were of one piece with it.

verses.rationale: Keeps six/three/three branch structure distinct from central shaft.

verses.rationale: Preserves repeated ornament formula and all-six extension rather than mechanically compressing literary pattern.
verses.before: Three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with bud and blossom, were on one branch, and three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with bud and blossom, on the next branch; so for the six branches coming out from the lampstand.
verses.after: One branch had three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a flower, and another branch had three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with a bud and a flower. All six branches extending from the lampstand were made this way.

verses.rationale: Keeps four on central lampstand distinct from three on each side branch.
verses.before: On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its buds and blossoms.
verses.after: The lampstand itself had four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its buds and flowers.
verses.tsw_comparator: On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with its buds and blossoms.

verses.rationale: Preserves threefold bud-beneath-two pattern and six total branches.
verses.before: A bud was under the first pair of branches coming from it, a bud under the second pair of branches coming from it, and a bud under the third pair of branches coming from it, for the six branches coming from it.

verses.rationale: Retains integral unity, hammered technique and purity.
verses.before: Their buds and branches were of one piece with it; all of it was one hammered work of pure gold.
verses.after: The buds and branches were of one piece with it, the whole lampstand hammered from a single piece of pure gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Their buds and branches were of one piece with it; all of it was one hammered work of pure gold.

verses.rationale: Keeps seven lamps and two utensil types with material specification.
verses.before: He made its seven lamps, its tongs, and its firepans of pure gold.
verses.after: He made its seven lamps, its tongs, and its firepans from pure gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made its seven lamps, its tongs, and its firepans of pure gold.

verses.rationale: Retains talent total covering both lampstand and all equipment.
verses.before: He made it and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.
verses.after: He made the lampstand and all its utensils from one talent of pure gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made it and all its utensils from a talent of pure gold.

verses.rationale: Preserves square one-by-one plan, two-cubit height and integral horns.

verses.after: He made the incense altar from acacia wood, a cubit long and a cubit wide, forming a square, and two cubits high. Its horns were of one piece with it.

verses.rationale: Retains every gilded surface and molding.

verses.after: He overlaid its top, all its sides, and its horns with pure gold, and made a gold molding around it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He overlaid it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns—and made a gold molding around it.

verses.rationale: Preserves two rings, below-molding placement and opposite sides without doubling to four.
verses.before: He made two rings of gold for it below its molding, on two opposite sides, as holders for poles with which to carry it.
verses.after: He made two gold rings for it beneath the molding, on its two opposite sides, to hold the poles used to carry it.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made two rings of gold for it below its molding, on two opposite sides, as holders for poles with which to carry it.

verses.rationale: Keeps repeated pole specification naturally without novelty quota.
verses.before: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
verses.after: He made the poles from acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the poles of acacia wood and overlaid them with gold.

verses.rationale: Preserves distinct holy/pure qualifiers and skilled perfumer role.

verses.after: He made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.
verses.tsw_comparator: He made the holy anointing oil and the pure fragrant incense, the work of a perfumer.

verses.rationale: Retains square five-by-five altar and three-cubit height distinct from incense altar.

verses.after: He made the altar of burnt offering from acacia wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide, forming a square, and three cubits high.

verses.rationale: Preserves five utensil kinds and repeated all-utensils bronze specification.

verses.rationale: Keeps rings on grating corners, count and carrying-pole purpose.

verses.after: He cast four rings at the four corners of the bronze grating to hold the poles.

verses.rationale: Retains bronze rather than importing gold pole material from inner furnishings.

verses.after: He made poles from acacia wood and overlaid them with bronze.
